auditor_value: ½gt² − (u sinθ)t + h = 0 has roots t₁, t₂ = [u sinθ ± √(u² sin²θ − 2gh)]/g; sum of roots t₁ + t₂ = 2u sinθ/g = T

findings.note: For ½gt² − (u sinθ)t + y₀ = 0 the discriminant is b² − 4ac = u²sin²θ − 4(½g)(y₀) = u²sin²θ − 2gy₀, not 4gy₀. The printed formula returns the two times at height 2y₀ (numeric check: u = 20, θ = 60°, y₀ = 5 gives roots at height 10 m), and at y₀ = H its discriminant is negative, contradicting this step's own text that two real roots exist for every height below the maximum. A student copying this root formula loses the mark whenever the individual times are asked.

notes: The final result t₁ + t₂ = 2u sinθ/g = T, the sum-of-roots reasoning in why_this_step (−b/a = 2u sinθ/g), and the product t₁t₂ = 2y₀/g in common_mistakes are all correct; only the explicit root formula in step 2 is false, and its error cancels in the sum, which is why the proof still lands on the right line.
